title: Baobab: Ancient Baobabs You Can Visit
meta_description: The African savannah tree that stores water in its trunk. Maria Gorda on Rio's Paquetá island is ten metres round and probably centuries old.
intro: Adansonia digitata belongs to the dry savannah of Africa, where it stores water in a swollen trunk and can live a thousand years. Carried across oceans, it puts on girth astonishingly fast. Honolulu's Foster Garden tree, nicknamed the Dead Rat Tree for its grey, furred seed pods, reached close to thirteen metres round in around ninety years. On the University of Hawaii's Manoa campus, the university built its new Art Building around a baobab in 1973 rather than move it. Brazil has the older ones. Maria Gorda, on the island of Paquetá in Rio de Janeiro, is ten metres round and probably centuries old, though its age is disputed, and a sign in front offers eternal luck to whoever kisses it. In Fortaleza, the city's Candomblé community venerates the baobab of the Passeio Público as sacred.
